- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior spike.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +10%+ from prior 30d avg) with negative sentiment, cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment turns positive after prolonged negativity, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 3–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3 in last 5 days.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model is lagging — adjust next forecast to match recent true trend, not historical mean.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model tends to overfit recent history — reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid mean reversion bias.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward correction by 1–3% per day to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
